title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the sequel to La Longue Marche. The setting is the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which is free of rank 2. It is extended by the S_3 of symmetries of the three points, generated by ρ (order 3) and σ_∞ (order 2), giving Π̃̂_{0,3}. The unknowns form the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type 'loop equation' data:
- f ∈ Π̂_{0,3} and ν ∈ Ẑ;
- elements g, h written as twisted coboundaries g = α ρ(α)^{-1} and h = β σ_∞(β)^{-1};
- auxiliary solutions ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} (case h = 1) and η = β_0 σ_∞(β_0)^{-1} (case g = 1);
- these are related on the previous page by (30) and (32), with l_0 = ε_0^2.

What this page does. Grothendieck tests these relations in an explicit matrix model. The discrete groups are realised as (P)GL(2,Z): Π_{0,3} is Γ(2)/±1 and its S_3-extension sits in PGL(2,Z). The profinite completion of the extended group is identified with GL(2,Z)'^, and all elements are pushed to the congruence quotient GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}/±1, keeping their names. Matrices in the quotient are known only up to sign, so he proposes to compute upstairs in GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1} (determinant ±1), lifting carefully.

Key observation. The lifts α, β, α_0, β_0 and f are defined only modulo ±1 (33, 35, 37). However, the expressions
- g = α ρ(α)^{-1} and h = β σ_∞(β)^{-1} (34),
- ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} and η = β_0 σ_∞(β_0)^{-1} (36),
- φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1} and ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1} (38),
are unaffected by α ↦ −α, because ρ(·) and σ_∞(·) are conjugations and the sign cancels. They are therefore well-defined elements of SL(2,Ẑ): the determinants cancel too.

Where it goes next. The next page notes that ε_0 = ±(1 −1; 0 1) is sign-ambiguous but l_0 = ε_0^2 = (1 −2; 0 1) is not. He then asks whether the relations ξ = l_0^ν φ (case h = 1) and η = l_0^{-ν} ψ (case g = 1) hold in SL(2,Ẑ) with a suitable sign. In short, the page reduces the loop equations to their image in the congruence (Legendre / level-2) quotient, to check sign consistency of the earlier formulas.
errors: The transcription's (34) 'g = αρα^{-1}, h = βρ_∞β^{-1}' should read g = αρ(α)^{-1}, h = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, consistent with (29) and (31) on the previous page. As transcribed, the formulas are not even of the intended coboundary form.
The phrase 'on est amené à calculer, non dans Gl(2,Ẑ), plutôt que de Gl(2,Ẑ)'' is garbled. The sense is: one must compute in Gl(2,Ẑ)^{±1} rather than in the quotient Gl(2,Ẑ)'.

Implicit caveat, not an error of Grothendieck: the profinite completion of PGL(2,Z) maps onto, but is not isomorphic to, PGL(2,Ẑ), because the congruence subgroup property fails. So the computations only see the congruence image of f, g, h, ξ, η. The page's wording 'images ... dans le quotient' is consistent with this.

ideas.what: Pushing the profinite loop-equation (GT-type) data from Π̂_{0,3} ⋊ S_3 to the congruence quotient GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 to compute explicitly with 2×2 matrices.
ideas.modern_name: Image of Grothendieck–Teichmüller / Galois data in the congruence (level-2, Legendre family) quotient of F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura and others (1980s–90s) for Galois action on quotients of F̂_2; Grothendieck's Longue Marche (1981) discusses the SL(2) picture
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated, later edited by Malgoire) treats related material

ideas.what: Sign ambiguity of lifts from PGL to GL^{±1} disappears for twisted coboundaries x·θ(x)^{-1} when θ is a conjugation; l_0 = ε_0^2 is canonical while ε_0 is not.
ideas.modern_name: Well-definedness of coboundaries under central ambiguity / canonical lift of squares

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical bookkeeping page about sign ambiguities when mapping loop-equation data to SL(2,Ẑ). The ideas are elementary and the overall framework (the GT loop equations and their image in congruence quotients) is known. Its only interest is as a witness of Grothendieck's explicit testing strategy.
transcription_corrections: 'on est amené à calculer, non dans Gl(2,Ẑ)' ...' probably reads 'on est amené à calculer dans Gl(2,Ẑ)^{±1} plutôt que dans Gl(2,Ẑ)''.
The group in line 1 is written as a hatted script letter with subscript 0,3 (probably the extended Teichmüller group of type (0,3)), not clearly 𝔖̂_{0,3}.
